title: AI tells -- rhetorical structure
description: Structure tells endure across model generations because preference training produces them: raters reward length, markdown, bulleted symmetry, and confident even-handedness, so every generation reconverges on the same shapes even as the vocabulary changes. Weight these above any word list.

citation.source: AI tells catalog — structure.md ("Contrastive inversion", "Strawman antithesis")
citation.note: The two-sentence form of the contrastive inversion: "X is A. X is not B." and its mirror, with the subject repeated or pronominalised. The single-sentence frame (ai-tells-structure.contrastive-inversion-frames) stops at a sentence boundary, so this rule runs at paragraph scope, where the native engine matches against the whole block (list items and quotes included; Vale's paragraph scope skips both, so the rule stays native). The negated half must open with a rhetorical marker ("about", "just", "whether", "because", ...) or with an article followed by one of the rhetorical nouns the tell reaches for ("a requirement", "an afterthought", "a checkbox", "a silver bullet", ...): "It is not configurable" states a property and does not fire, and neither does a definitional distinction over concrete nouns ("The lock is a lease. It is not a mutex."), which the first version of this rule caught 15 times in 15 constructed legitimate sentences. Measured in the 2026-09-12 audit and its follow-up: 0 hits in 21k parsed words of pre-2022 human prose and 30k of gated prose; every one of the 5 model-corpus hits kept; 1 of 15 legitimate distinctions fires (an acknowledgement that "is not a guarantee"), down from 15; 8 of 12 constructed tells fire, the 4 missed being the same-shape concrete-noun forms that the reviewer's judgement remainder covers. Warning, never error, with a `factual-correction` exception for the sentence a writer keeps.

citation.note: Judgement remainder of ai-tells-structure.absolute-assertion-core. Preserve quotations, attributed claims, and factual descriptions tied to a named person, work, edition, document, product, or other explicit finite set; local all/only/never inherits its stated antecedent; and preserve bounded comparative recommendations. Flag unsupported authorial guarantees or categorical evaluations (including "will tell you", "wherever ... has a problem", or "you are wrong") and sweeping always/never/every/no X has ever claims unless attributed or supported by quantified or passage evidence. The local-never preservation excludes a component described by an action it never takes: "The release agent never merges a pull request" has a stated antecedent, so the preservation passed that form, and prose-discipline.negative-guarantee-remainder now judges it.

examples.bad: Outside a run the plugin spawns no process.

rules.fix: State what the component does. Where the limit matters, name what enforces it (a hook, test, gate, lock, or permission); otherwise delete the sentence. In agent guidance, write the limit as a directive. Review modal and passive guarantees with prose-discipline.negative-guarantee-remainder.

citation.note: Matches descriptive "X never acts", listed side-effect verbs with "no", and "does/do not ever". Subjects have at most seven words and start at a sentence or clause boundary, or a capitalised pronoun or determiner. Paragraph scope includes list items, quotes, and table cells. Modal guarantees and passive constructions belong to prose-discipline.negative-guarantee-remainder. That question preserves explained guarantees and language, protocol, or data invariants. The core skips normative modals, imperatives, selected state verbs, and selected past-tense forms. Its active forms can still match a backed invariant; use the enforced-invariant exception when the passage names its enforcement. The rule reports a warning at normal and strict, and a suggestion at relaxed.

rules.name: Explain the mechanism instead of the metaphor
rules.message: teacher voice: {match} -- explain the actual mechanism once; cut the teacher voice

examples.bad: Think of it like a highway system for data.
examples.good: The bus fans one message out to every registered handler.

rules.fix: State the mechanism once and delete the analogy.

citation.note: Mechanizable core. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-structure.think-of-it-as-remainder, because an analogy can be introduced with no frame at all.

rules.name: Judge whether an analogy replaces the mechanism
rules.message: teacher voice: explain the actual mechanism once

match.question: Is the mechanism stated anywhere in this passage, or does the analogy stand in place of it?

examples.bad: The scheduler is the traffic warden of the cluster.
examples.good: The scheduler assigns each pod to the node with the most free memory.

rules.fix: State the mechanism; keep the analogy only if it shortens the explanation.

citation.note: Judgement remainder of ai-tells-structure.think-of-it-as-core.

rules.name: List the actual items or name the real dimension
rules.message: false range: list the actual items, or name the real dimension

match.question: Do the two endpoints of this "from X to Y" construction sit on a real scale, or are they two unordered members of a set?

examples.bad: from beef to chicken
examples.good: beef, chicken, and pork

examples.bad: from startups to enterprises
examples.good: teams of 3 to 3,000 engineers

rules.fix: List the items, or name the dimension that actually varies.

citation.note: A pattern for "from X to Y" would fire on every legitimate range, so this is judgement-only: the test is whether the endpoints are ordered, which needs the reader to know the domain.

rules.name: Name the source or own the claim
rules.message: vague attribution: {match} -- name the source or own the claim

examples.bad: Experts agree that lockfiles reduce drift.
examples.good: The npm RFC 0012 measured a 40% drop in resolution variance with a lockfile.

rules.fix: Name the source with a citation, or state the claim in your own voice.

citation.note: Mechanizable core, enforced at every tier: an unsourced appeal to authority is a factual defect in any register, and .vale.ini already keeps upstream ai-tells.VagueAttributions at error even for source comments. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-structure.vague-attribution-remainder. This is the one structure rule the source config already trusted enough to gate code comments on.

rules.name: Judge whether a cited source is checkable
rules.message: vague attribution: name the source or own the claim

match.question: Could a reader locate the source behind this claim from what the sentence gives them?

examples.bad: The literature is clear on this.
examples.good: RFC 7231 section 6.5.1 defines the status code.

rules.fix: Add the citation, or restate the claim as your own.

citation.note: Judgement remainder of ai-tells-structure.vague-attribution-core. Also the checkability half of content-shape's fabricated-citation entry -- see ai-tells-content-shape.fabricated-citations-remainder.

rules.name: Write for the one audience the doc has
rules.message: audience straddle: {match} -- write for the one audience the doc has

examples.bad: Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned pro, this guide has something for you.
examples.good: This guide assumes you have run `apm install` once.

rules.fix: Pick the audience the document has and write for it.

citation.note: Mechanizable core. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-structure.audience-straddle-remainder covers the case where the straddle is implicit -- a page that defines `git commit` and then discusses rebase strategy.

rules.name: Judge whether the document holds one audience
rules.message: audience straddle: write for the one audience the doc has

match.question: Does the document make one reader switch between a primer and expert operational detail without a single task that requires both? Flag the straddle when removing either half leaves the current task and contract intact. Keep definitions needed for the stated task, and keep audience changes that are explicit in a change communication, decision, plan, or specification.

examples.bad: A commit is a snapshot. Later: rebase onto the upstream to linearise the DAG.
examples.good: Rebase onto the upstream to linearise the history.

examples.bad: This guide defines HTTP, then assumes you can diagnose a TLS handshake.
examples.good: Diagnose the TLS handshake with `openssl s_client`.
This release note gives the migration steps and then records the old behavior.
examples.bad: Whether you are a beginner or an expert, every part of this guide is for you.

rules.fix: Pick the audience for the task and cut material that cannot help complete it.
